record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: Beyond the classical Jacobi, Laguerre, and Hermite cases, can one construct analogous electrostatic models for other families of polynomials in which the zeros are realized as equilibrium configurations of interacting charges under an explicit external field?

evidence.quote: • are there generalizations of these models to other families of polynomials?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For the classical orthogonal polynomial families (Jacobi, Laguerre, Hermite), Stieltjes proved that the zeros admit an electrostatic interpretation: namely, the zeros of the n-th polynomial can be realized as the equilibrium configuration of n unit positive charges confined to a fixed real interval (or the real line) which mutually repel via a logarithmic Coulomb potential and which interact with an explicit external field generated by fixed charges and/or a long-range confining potential determined by the weight function. More precisely, if w(x) = e^{-V(x)} is the weight and x_1,…,x_n are the zeros, then (x_1,…,x_n) is a critical point of the energy
   E(t_1,…,t_n) = sum_{i<j} log(1/|t_i - t_j|) + (1/2) sum_i V(t_i).

Problem. Identify and construct electrostatic models for other families of polynomials beyond the classical Jacobi, Laguerre, and Hermite cases. That is: for a given family of polynomials {P_n}_{n≥0} (for example, semiclassical orthogonal polynomials, Sobolev-type orthogonal polynomials, multiple orthogonal polynomials, exceptional orthogonal polynomials, or Heine–Stieltjes polynomials), produce a configuration space, a system of mutually interacting (logarithmic) charges, and an explicit external field Φ such that the zeros of P_n appear exactly as an equilibrium (critical point of the total energy) of this charge system. Determine for which families such a model exists, give an explicit formula for the external field Φ in terms of the data defining the family, and characterize the type of equilibrium (minimum, saddle, etc.) attained by the zeros.
artifact.category_tag: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: electrostatic models have been constructed for semiclassical weights, multiple orthogonal polynomials (Hermite–Padé type II), Laguerre–Sobolev and other Sobolev-type polynomials, and quasi-orthogonal polynomials, via second-order ODE techniques. A fully general framework that covers all families of interest (including, e.g., exceptional orthogonal polynomials and arbitrary nonclassical settings) and that characterizes the nature of the equilibrium is still being actively developed, so the broad problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic Partners and Zeros of Orthogonal and Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: For multiple orthogonal polynomials of type II, the approach yields a system of linear second-order differential equations, from which an electrostatic interpretation of their zeros can be derived.
status_evidence.claim: Electrostatic interpretation extended to multiple orthogonal polynomials.

status_evidence.title: An electrostatic model for zeros of general orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: For a given polynomial P with simple zeros and a given semiclassical weight w, an ODE can be constructed that yields an electrostatic model for zeros of P.
status_evidence.claim: General construction exists for semiclassical weights.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic Models for Zeros of Laguerre–Sobolev Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Electrostatic models for Laguerre–Sobolev polynomial zeros are derived.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic Interpretation of Zeros of Orthogonal Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of electrostatic interpretations beyond the classical cases.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area with continuing generalizations.
